predicted_disagreements: Shannon vs Turing, axis source-corpus + methodology: Shannon runs inventory/semantic evidence and can over-trust recorded language; Turing runs executable validators and exposes that bias by demoting any phrase not backed by runnable deterministic checks. Shannon exposes Turing's too-narrow tool bias by surfacing cited evidence from inventory/query findings that a script-only audit would miss.

Shannon vs Grothendieck, axis source-corpus + methodology: Shannon runs proof/moat inventory entries and can treat claims as evidence; Grothendieck runs Lean/formal witness status and exposes that bias by separating machine-checked witness, theorem, open sorry, and prose claim. Shannon exposes Grothendieck's formal-isolation bias by showing where formal artifacts matter only through surrounding commercialization/evidence context.

Turing vs Grothendieck, axis methodology: Turing runs deterministic validators/audits and can collapse structural checks into proof language; Grothendieck runs formal semantics/proof status and exposes that bias by requiring exact proof-obligation labels. Turing exposes Grothendieck's proof-purity bias by identifying runnable deterministic witness value that is commercially useful before a full theorem.
